company.oneLiner: Storywell turns guided family conversations into a private, searchable audio archive.
company.thesis: Families value the stories of older relatives, but recording them feels awkward, time-consuming, and technically intimidating. A guided mobile experience can make preservation feel natural enough to become a habit.
company.targetCustomer: Adult children ages 35 to 55 who live apart from a parent or grandparent and feel urgency about preserving family stories.
company.problem: People postpone meaningful family interviews until it is too late because they do not know what to ask, how to record well, or how to organize the result.
company.solution: A private mobile app that schedules short guided prompts, records calls or in-person conversations, transcribes them, and organizes the archive by person, topic, and era.
company.positioning: The easiest way to preserve the voice and stories of the people who made your family.
company.differentiation: Storywell combines guided interviewing, family participation, and a durable private archive. It is not a generic recorder, genealogy database, or public social network.
company.businessModel: Consumer subscription with one family workspace and up to eight contributors.
company.pricing: $79 per year after a 14-day trial; founding-family price under review.
company.northStarMetric: Families that save three meaningful stories in their first 14 days.
company.currentGoal: Reach a decision-grade beta with 20 active families and evidence of repeat recording behavior.
constraints: Must earn trust with older participants

workstreams.title: Business thesis
workstreams.summary: Define the wedge, strategic choices, and what the company will not be.
workstreams.nextAction: Lock the first-year wedge around adult-child initiated family interviews.
workstreams.rationale: The thesis is coherent, but the product still carries traces of three adjacent businesses: genealogy, podcasting, and family social networking.
facts: The founder is building iOS first.
The launch team is two people.
assumptions: Adult children will initiate and pay for the family archive.
Private preservation is a stronger wedge than public storytelling.
questions: Should the paying customer be the interviewer, the family, or a gift purchaser?

workstreams.title: Customer and problem
workstreams.summary: Choose a primary buyer and understand the moment that creates urgency.
workstreams.nextAction: Interview five people who recently lost or moved a parent into care.
workstreams.rationale: The emotional problem is strong, but the current evidence over-indexes on friends who already value family history.
assumptions: A recent health event or milestone creates enough urgency to overcome interview discomfort.
The adult child is willing to coordinate other relatives.
questions: Which trigger produces the shortest path from interest to first recording?

workstreams.title: Market and competition
workstreams.summary: Understand substitutes, category language, and credible market size.
workstreams.nextAction: Complete a substitute map using voice recorder, Storyworth, and genealogy workflows.
workstreams.rationale: Competitor feature tables exist, but the more useful question is what people do instead of buying anything.
facts: The category includes interview services, prompt subscriptions, genealogy products, and generic recorders.
assumptions: Trust and ease of contribution matter more than transcription novelty.
questions: How often does the customer choose a one-time gift instead of an ongoing archive?

workstreams.title: Product and offer
workstreams.summary: Define the smallest product that delivers the promised outcome.
workstreams.nextAction: Cut public sharing and AI-written memoir features from the beta scope.
workstreams.rationale: The core capture and archive loop is clear. Secondary delight features are diluting the first-value path.
facts: Clickable prototype testing is complete with six participants.
assumptions: A guided prompt is enough to start a 10-minute recording.
questions: Does asynchronous contribution outperform scheduled live interviews?

workstreams.title: Business model and pricing
workstreams.summary: Choose the offer, pricing logic, and unit-economic assumptions.
workstreams.nextAction: Choose annual subscription versus one-time family archive before paywall design begins.
workstreams.rationale: The current pricing language mixes a recurring service with a finite preservation project. That contradiction will confuse both acquisition and retention.
facts: Storage and transcription costs are low at the current expected usage.
assumptions: Families will accept annual pricing for continued access and contributions.
questions: Is the natural purchase a subscription, gift, or lifetime archive?

workstreams.title: Brand and positioning
workstreams.summary: Create a credible promise and a consistent verbal and visual system.
workstreams.nextAction: Replace nostalgic category language with a more active preservation promise.
workstreams.rationale: The current brand is warm, but some copy sounds like memorial software rather than a living family ritual.
assumptions: Calm and private will convert better than playful and social.
questions: Can the brand communicate urgency without becoming morbid?

workstreams.title: Go-to-market
workstreams.summary: Build a repeatable path to the first qualified families.
workstreams.nextAction: Recruit the first 20 families through caregiving and family-history communities.
workstreams.rationale: A channel list exists, but there is no narrow launch motion with a named audience, message, and conversion event.
facts: The founder has access to two local caregiver communities.
assumptions: Community partnerships will outperform paid social for the first cohort.
questions: What event or resource earns enough trust for a family to upload its first voice recording?

workstreams.title: Launch plan
workstreams.summary: Turn the strategy into sequenced milestones, proof, and owner accountability.
workstreams.nextAction: Resolve pricing and privacy blockers before committing the App Store date.
workstreams.rationale: Product progress is ahead of the business decisions required to launch it responsibly.
facts: The target beta date is October 1, 2026.
assumptions: Twenty active families are enough for a launch decision.
questions: Which launch gates are mandatory for a private family archive?
